Publish puts the rodeo in a public GitHub repository of yours and opens a pull request on rodeo-cli that adds it to the rodeo catalog (rodeo/data/catalog.d/<name>.yaml: name, title, repository, ref, engine, languages). The repository holds the files of the download.

  • rodeo builder on loopback uses the GitHub login already on its host, without storing it: GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, else the GitHub CLI's login (gh auth token), else git's stored github.com credential. With none, Log in to GitHub runs gh auth login --web and shows its one-time code to enter at github.com/login/device; without gh, install it, run gh auth login or set GH_TOKEN before rodeo builder. Publishing creates github.com/<you>/<name>, pushes one commit on main, forks rodeo-cli when you don't own it and opens the catalog pull request. Update my existing repository pushes a new commit that replaces the files (the repository's .github/ stays) and opens no pull request. RODEO_CATALOG_REPO points the pull request at another repository.

Translations go to language branches. main holds the source language (story.language: en). Each translated language gets a branch named after it: main plus that language's story/strings/<lang>/, with story.language: <lang>. On an update, an existing language branch only gets its story/strings/<lang>/ replaced. main also gets .github/workflows/rodeo-languages.yml: on every push to main, it opens a pull request main → <lang> for each language branch that is behind main (the check of rodeo story check), and you resolve any conflicts in it. Publish lets the repository's Actions open those pull requests (Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests). The result lists the language branches and warns about anything left out: the workflow, when the GitHub login can't write workflows (it needs the workflow scope); that setting, when GitHub refuses it; a language branch that couldn't be pushed. - The published page (and rodeo builder --expose) links to github.com pages that use your browser's GitHub login, and GitHub asks you to log in when you aren't: create the repository, upload the unzipped download (or git push), and add the catalog file, which forks rodeo-cli and opens the pull request under your account.

docs.title: How the published page is built
docs.text:
The published page is the live page's static subset. scripts/build-builder-static.py embeds what rodeo/builder/api.py answers (engines and bundled chapters from rodeo/data/, the chapter sources' chapters, and the catalogue of lab-in-a-box's latest release) into the page and marks it static, which hides Save to profiles; the docs workflow publishes it at builder/. The build fetches each chapter source with a shallow, sparse git clone (only the chapter files and check scripts) and fails if one can't be fetched, or if the lab-in-a-box catalogue can't be read. Build it locally:

python3 scripts/build-builder-static.py --output /tmp/builder --labinabox /path/to/lab-in-a-box
python3 -m http.server -d /tmp/builder 8000

--source <id>=<checkout> uses a local checkout for one chapter source, --no-fetch-sources builds without them (offline), and --no-labinabox builds without the lab-in-a-box catalogue (the page then shows it as unavailable).

docs.title: Operations runbook
docs.text: Quick reference for diagnosing and recovering from problems in a deployed rodeo lab. Each section starts with how to confirm the problem and then covers the fix.

docs.title: Deploy failed mid-pipeline
docs.text:
Confirm: rodeo status shows a red phase. The terminal output has an error message.

Fix: identify the failed phase and resume:

rodeo status                      # find the last failed phase
rodeo deploy --from <phase>       # resume from there

If you are not sure what changed, force a full re-run of the failed phase:

rodeo deploy --from kvm_host --force   # re-run everything from phase kvm_host

Look back at a run: every deploy appends its events to <lab>/.rodeo/events.jsonl (mode 0600), one JSON object per line, with known secret values masked:

jq -r 'select(.kind=="PhaseFailed") | "\(.phase) rc=\(.rc) \(.text)"' .rodeo/events.jsonl

Schema v0: ts (Unix time), lab (lab realpath), phase (null before the first phase), kind (PhaseStarted, PhaseSkipped, PhaseDone, PhaseFailed, LogLine, ProgressUpdate, DeployComplete), text (log line, failure message, skip reason or progress step), rc (PhaseFailed only), elapsed (seconds, PhaseDone and ProgressUpdate) and v (0). At 10 MB the file moves to events.jsonl.1, replacing the older one. rodeo writes it relative to the lab's directory and refuses a symlink or hard link there; a write that fails is logged once and never stops the deploy.

docs.title: Harvester install appears stuck: stuck vs timed out
docs.text:
Context: the cluster phase waits up to 60 minutes for the Harvester VIP to come up. On nested KVM this can take 45–90 minutes. The question is whether the install is still making progress or has genuinely hung.

Step 1: check the heartbeat file:

cat ~/.rodeo/logs/<lab-name>-heartbeat.txt

rodeo writes this file every 5 minutes during the VIP and node-ready waits. It records VM states and elapsed time. If the file exists and the timestamp is recent (< 6 min old), the deploy is alive. If the file is missing or stale, the host process may have died.

Step 2: check VM states:

virsh list --all
  • All running = install in progress (normal). Watch rodeo logs harvester1 for kernel/installer output.
  • All shut off = installer exited early. Check the serial log for the error:
rodeo logs harvester1
  • Any paused = memory pressure on the host. Free RAM or add swap, then virsh resume <vm>.

Step 3: distinguish a stuck install from an Instruqt session timeout:

Instruqt terminates the GCP lab VM (not just the browser session) after the platform-configured idle timeout. If the lab VM is gone, there is no reconnecting, the install cannot have "hung" because the host no longer exists.

Signs the lab was terminated (not stuck): - virsh list --all fails with "failed to connect to the hypervisor" - SSH to the Instruqt host times out entirely - The heartbeat file is missing or from a previous run

Signs the install is genuinely stuck: - VMs are running, heartbeat is fresh, but serial log has not scrolled for > 15 minutes - Serial log shows a repeating error (disk full, interface not found, etcd election loop)

Common install hang causes:

Symptom in serial log Cause Fix no network interface found or hangs at network config Interface name mismatch: installer got a config naming eth0 but kernel uses ens3 Wipe VMs (rodeo deploy --from vms --force) and redeploy curl: (7) Failed to connect to config URL nginx not running or virbr0 not up Check nginx: rodeo ssh <host> -- sudo systemctl status nginx Disk full / containerd errors VM disk too small (Elemental's persistent partition floor is a fixed 150 GiB) Redeploy with disk_gb: 320 in plan etcd election loop, node never joins Rapid join race on 3-node setup Increase etcd_join_gap_seconds in definition.yaml (default: 90)

docs.title: Harvester VIP not responding
docs.text:
Symptom: the cluster phase times out waiting for 192.168.122.10:443.

Confirm:

rodeo logs harvester1   # is the installer still running?

If the log is still progressing (you see kernel messages or the Harvester installer), wait: on hosts with slower disks it can take 45–90 minutes on nested KVM.

If the log is stuck or empty:

rodeo ssh harvester1              # connect to the node
sudo journalctl -u rke2-server -f # check RKE2 status

Common causes and fixes:

Cause Fix Disk too small Clean and redeploy with disk_gb: 320 in the plan Not enough RAM rodeo doctor to check; free up RAM or use a smaller profile pxe_server served wrong config Check nginx logs: rodeo ssh <host> -- sudo journalctl -u nginx etcd join race The 90s etcd_join_gap_seconds prevents this; check if it was reduced

docs.title: Host port-forward not working (host:8443 / host:30002)
docs.text:
Symptom: https://<host>:8443 times out from outside, but https://192.168.122.10:443 works from inside the host.

Confirm:

# On the host:
sudo nft list table ip libvirt_network   # look for the guest_input chain

If the guest_input chain has a reject rule but no ct status dnat accept rule before it, the libvirt hook is missing or did not fire.

Fix:

sudo /etc/libvirt/hooks/network default started   # re-apply the DNAT rule

If the hook file is missing (e.g. after a kvm_host phase that did not complete):

rodeo deploy --from kvm_host --force   # reinstalls the hook

docs.title: Secrets not resolved
docs.text:
Symptom: deploy fails immediately with unresolved credential or empty password.

Fix:

# Regenerate secrets
rodeo init --force
# Then retry deploy
rodeo deploy --from kvm_host --force

Or edit ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml directly and add the missing keys.

docs.title: "python3-lxml not found" error
docs.text:
Symptom: the vms Ansible phase fails with a missing lxml module error.

Fix:

sudo rodeo install-deps   # installs python3-lxml alongside other host packages

Then resume:

rodeo deploy --from vms

docs.title: VM stuck in paused state
docs.text:
Confirm:

virsh list --all   # shows STATE = paused

Fix:

virsh resume <vm-name>
# or via rodeo:
rodeo restart <vm-name>

If it re-pauses immediately, check host RAM: the hypervisor pauses VMs when memory pressure is critical.

docs.title: etcd member broken (one node lost)
docs.text:
This happens if a Harvester VM was force-deleted or its disk corrupted while the cluster was running.

Confirm from a healthy node:

rodeo ssh harvester2
# Inside the VM:
ETCD_CERT=/var/lib/rancher/rke2/server/tls/etcd
crictl exec $(crictl ps --name etcd -q) etcdctl \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=$ETCD_CERT/server-ca.crt \
  --cert=$ETCD_CERT/server-client.crt \
  --key=$ETCD_CERT/server-client.key \
  member list

If one member shows unstarted or is missing:

Recovery (3 steps):

# Step 1: remove the broken member from a healthy node
MEMBER_ID=<id from member list>
crictl exec <etcd-container-id> etcdctl \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=$ETCD_CERT/server-ca.crt \
  --cert=$ETCD_CERT/server-client.crt \
  --key=$ETCD_CERT/server-client.key \
  member remove $MEMBER_ID

# Step 2: on the broken node, wipe the etcd data and add a rejoin config
rodeo ssh harvester1   # or whichever node is broken
sudo rm -rf /var/lib/rancher/rke2/server/db/etcd
sudo tee /etc/rancher/rke2/config.yaml.d/00-rejoin.yaml <<EOF
server: https://192.168.122.10:9345
token: $(grep harvester_token ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
EOF

# Step 3: restart rke2-server on the broken node
sudo systemctl restart rke2-server
# Wait ~3 minutes, then verify:
kubectl get nodes   # all should be Ready

docs.title: libvirt not starting
docs.text:
Symptom: virsh list fails with a connection error.

Confirm:

systemctl status virtqemud.socket virtnetworkd.socket

SLES 16 uses modular libvirt (socket-activated daemons), not the monolithic libvirtd. If the sockets are inactive:

sudo systemctl enable --now virtqemud.socket virtnetworkd.socket virtstoraged.socket

docs.title: virbr0 missing after host reboot
docs.text:
Symptom: VMs cannot start because virbr0 does not exist.

Cause: libvirt-guests was not enabled (the finalise phase was skipped or failed), so libvirt did not start automatically.

Fix:

sudo virsh net-start default
sudo virsh net-autostart default

Or re-run finalise:

rodeo deploy --from finalise --finalise

docs.title: Accidentally destroyed the virbr0 network with virsh
docs.text:
Symptom: ran virsh net-destroy default while the cluster was running. All VM network connectivity is lost.

Fix (restore connectivity without VM restart):

# Re-create the bridge and reattach tap devices
sudo ip link set virbr0 up
for tap in $(virsh domiflist harvester1 | awk '/vnet/{print $1}') \
           $(virsh domiflist harvester2 | awk '/vnet/{print $1}') \
           $(virsh domiflist harvester3 | awk '/vnet/{print $1}'); do
    sudo ip link set $tap master virbr0
    sudo ip link set $tap up
done
sudo ip neigh flush dev virbr0

# Restart the libvirt network (re-applies DNAT rules and firewall hook)
sudo virsh net-start default
sudo /etc/libvirt/hooks/network default started

Verify connectivity:

ping -c 3 192.168.122.11   # harvester1
ping -c 3 192.168.122.10   # VIP

If VMs lost their cluster state, you may need to recover etcd (see above).

docs.title: Full host reset
docs.text:
Use this when you want to start over completely, wipes all lab VMs, disks, state, and credentials, but leaves packages and the rodeo binary:

rodeo stop --all --yes 2>/dev/null || true   # graceful stop first
rodeo clean --all --yes --secrets --force-network

Then deploy fresh:

rodeo up --profile <name>

docs.title: Collect a support bundle
docs.text:
rodeo logs --bundle -o rodeo-bundle.tar.gz

The bundle includes: redacted plan (secrets replaced with ***), phase state, recent serial log tails for all VMs, and virsh domain info. Attach it when filing a bug or escalating to maintainers.

docs.title: Multi-host workshop failures
docs.text:
For fleet deploys, pick the failing host from the job file or rodeo fleet status, then pull forensics to the laptop:

rodeo fleet diagnose -f workshop.yaml                  # failed hosts (default)
rodeo fleet diagnose -f workshop.yaml --all-selected   # every selected host

See Fleet: Diagnose for the artifact layout.

docs.title: "This machine cannot host labs" / "not a supported KVM host"
docs.text:
Confirm: rodeo up or rodeo deploy stops with macOS cannot host labs or <distribution> is not a supported KVM host.

Why: labs run on SLES 16 / Leap 16 only. Any other machine is a control machine: it drives hosts on AWS or over SSH but never runs a lab itself.

Fix: deploy to the cloud from that machine, or run rodeo on a SLES 16 host:

rodeo up --profile <name> --target aws

RODEO_ALLOW_ANY_KVM_HOST=1 lets you try a local lab on another Linux anyway, unsupported.

docs.title: Install fails with setuptools>=68 or another pip error
docs.text:
Confirm: install.sh stops while setting up the Python environment, often on SLES/Leap 15 (Python 3.6).

Fix: re-run the current installer. Since v0.22 it installs a control machine on those systems, with a Python 3.10+ it finds or a private one it downloads, and it rebuilds the broken environment:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avaleror/rodeo-cli/main/install.sh | bash

docs.title: AWS: start a deploy and come back later
docs.text:
rodeo up --target aws --detach returns as soon as the host has started rodeo up. It prints one JSON line (pid, log, host) and the deploy keeps running on the host. Check on it from the lab directory:

rodeo status --cloud            # running / exited N / gone / none, plus the last 40 log lines
rodeo status --cloud --lines 200 --output json

gone means the recorded process is dead without an exit code (killed, or the host rebooted). A second rodeo up --target aws while one runs stops with exit 75. Without --detach, rodeo up --target aws waits and follows the log as before.

--detach works the same way for gcp and for deployment_target: remote. The files on the host are gcp-up.log or remote-up.log, with .pid and .exit beside them. rodeo status --cloud reads whichever this plan deploys to. A remote plan names the host. rodeo does not create it and does not destroy it.

The MCP server detaches aws only. A gcp or remote deploy started from rodeo_up blocks until the host finishes. rodeo_status with cloud: true can still read a detached run.

docs.title: AWS: login, region and capacity errors
docs.text: Message Fix session has expired / CreateOAuth2Token Run aws login again. A transient CreateOAuth2Token error mid-command can also just need a re-run. MissingDependencyException The [aws] extra is missing (boto3[crt]). Re-run install.sh, which installs it on control machines. no default VPC in <region> That region has no default VPC. Export RODEO_AWS_REGION to one that has, or set provider.region and provider.subnet_id in the plan. not offered in region / not enough capacity Try another region or --instance-tier, or pin provider.instance_type. rodeo never downsizes on its own. has no public IP / no internet route The subnet does not route to an internet gateway. Pick a public subnet.

docs.title: AWS: lab unreachable or host gone
docs.text:
UI or SSH times out from your laptop. rodeo's security group only admits the public IP you had when the host was created. If your IP changed (new network, VPN), re-run rodeo up --target aws from the lab directory: it moves the rule to your current IP and skips phases already done.

The host disappeared during a session. The dead-man switch terminated it: every cloud host expires provider.ttl_hours after launch (6 by default), shown as Self-destructs at the end of rodeo up and in the rodeo-expires-at instance tag. Re-deploy, and set a longer provider.ttl_hours before creating hosts for long sessions.

Is anything still billing? Tear down with rodeo destroy --cloud --yes --config-dir <lab dir> (or rodeo fleet deprovision for a fleet). Both also remove the local leftovers of the terminated hosts (host keys, student keys, ~/.rodeo/fleet/<name>/), so a new instance that reuses an IP never trips a stale host key. To check every region for leftovers:

for r in $(aws ec2 describe-regions --query 'Regions[].RegionName' --output text); do
  aws ec2 describe-instances --region "$r" \
    --filters Name=tag:ManagedBy,Values=rodeo Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running,stopping,stopped \
    --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].[InstanceId,InstanceType,State.Name]' --output text
done

docs.title: sudo rodeo / sudo ssh -i /root/.ssh/id_ed25519 ... says "command not found"
docs.text:
SUSE's default /usr/etc/sudoers ships two conflicting Defaults secure_path= lines; the second (narrower, missing /usr/local/*) wins, so sudo can't find rodeo (installed under /usr/local/bin) even though it works fine without sudo. The kvm_host phase fixes this automatically on SUSE hosts (see /etc/sudoers.d/rodeo-secure-path) starting with a fresh rodeo deploy.

If you hit this on a host with VMs already running, don't re-run --from kvm_host just for this: on a live lab that phase also re-touches firewalld and the libvirt network, which can conflict with domains that are already up. Apply the one-off fix directly instead:

echo 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"' \
  | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/rodeo-secure-path >/dev/null
sudo visudo -c   # confirm it parses before trusting it

docs.text: Historical snapshot (2026-07-14). Findings below reflect the tree at that date. For the current docs-only re-audit, see audit-2026-08-05.md.

docs.title: rodeo-cli code audit — 2026-07-14
docs.text:
Technical audit of /Users/avalero/GitHub/rodeo-cli against CLAUDE.md, ROADMAP.md, CONTEXT.md, and the live codebase. Conducted before a fix pass; issues are ordered by severity with suggested remediation.

Repo state at audit time: main @ v0.12.0 · ruff clean · 188/190 tests passing locally (Python 3.14; 2 brittle assertion failures from Rich ANSI markup).

docs.title: Executive summary
docs.text: Area Verdict Architecture Solid declarative-deployment model; main debt is phase-level vs resource-level idempotency Code quality Good modularity in commands/profiles; rancher.py is a maintainability hotspot Tests Strong unit suite; 2 brittle failures locally; no automated KVM integration in CI Docs CONTEXT.md / CLAUDE.md lag behind main (v0.12.0, ~190 tests) Production readiness Bare-metal validated for most profiles; Instruqt queue largely pending

docs.title: 1. Phase-level idempotency hides resource drift (known, documented)
docs.text:
DeployRunner.run() skips any phase marked completed in state, without checking whether the host still matches the plan:

# rodeo/engine/runner.py
if not self.force and is_phase_done(phase, self._plan_name):
    yield PhaseSkipped(phase, "done")
    continue

rodeo plan detects VM memory/vCPU drift, but rodeo deploy / rodeo up ignore it unless the user passes --force or --from. Tracked as ROADMAP Phase B2.

Risk: Silent no-op after plan edits — looks successful, nothing changes.

Remediation: Extract drift detection from plan_cmd.py into rodeo/drift.py; wire --reconcile into DeployRunner (opt-in first, default later). V1 scope: VM memory/vCPU only; topology changes deferred.

docs.title: 2. Split ~/.rodeo ownership under sudo (real bug)
docs.text:
Secrets resolution correctly uses the invoking user's home via _invoking_home() in config.py, but state, logs, kubeconfig, and the success screen use bare Path.home():

Path Under sudo rodeo up Secrets (load) /home/user/.rodeo/secrets.yaml ✓ State /root/.rodeo/state/ ✗ Logs /root/.rodeo/logs/ ✗ Kubeconfig /root/.rodeo/harvester-kubeconfig ✗ Success screen passwords reads /root/.rodeo/secrets.yaml ✗

Affected modules: state.py, secretgen.py, success.py, runner.py, cluster.py, clean.py, init_cmd.py, generate_cmd.py, config.py (_LAST_LAB_FILE).

Symptom: After rodeo up (self-escalates for deploy), rodeo status / rodeo plan as the normal user may show empty phase state; the success screen may not display passwords even though deploy succeeded.

Remediation: Centralize rodeo_home() using _invoking_home() / home_of_invoking_user() for every path under ~/.rodeo.

Status: Fixed — see rodeo/paths.py and fix log below.

docs.title: 3. Instruqt download fragility — get_url still used in PXE path
docs.text:
rancher_image.yml correctly uses curl -4 --http1.1 (Instruqt-safe), but Harvester PXE artifacts and the ISO download still use Ansible get_url:

  • rodeo/data/ansible/roles/vms/tasks/images.yml — Harvester ISO
  • rodeo/data/ansible/roles/pxe_server/tasks/files.yml — vmlinuz, initrd, rootfs

On Instruqt hosts with AAAA records and no IPv6 routing, Python urllib tries IPv6 first → errno 101 Network unreachable. Documented in CLAUDE.md but not fixed on all paths.

Remediation: Port the curl -4 --http1.1 shell pattern from rancher_image.yml to images.yml and pxe_server/tasks/files.yml.

docs.title: 4. plan diff uses wrong flavors for non-Harvester VMs
docs.text:
# rodeo/commands/plan_cmd.py
def _flavor_of(cfg: dict, vm: str) -> dict:
    flavor = "rancher" if vm == "rancher" else "harvester"
    return cfg.get("resources", {}).get(flavor, {})

For suse-edge, VMs like eib, edge1–edge4 are compared against harvester resources instead of eib / edge-node. inventory.py notes plan should derive flavor from inventory — wiring never completed.

Risk: rodeo plan reports false "unchanged" or misses real drift on edge labs.

Remediation: Derive flavor per VM from cfg["vms"] + inventory vm_nodes, or from build_inventory() output.

docs.title: 5. rancher.py is a 1,910-line monolith
docs.text:
Almost all Rancher/K3s/Elemental/import logic lives in one file. ROADMAP.md defers splitting into api.py + remote.py. Works today but highest regression risk for Rancher phase changes.

Two poll loops use raw time.sleep() instead of self._sleep(), breaking cancellation:

# rodeo/engine/rancher.py (~1359, ~1412)
time.sleep(10)
time.sleep(15)

Remediation: Split module (later); replace time.sleep with self._sleep (quick win).

docs.title: 6. Network idempotency guard — coarse and unvalidated live
docs.text: roles/vms/tasks/network_setup.yml only checks that some <host mac= reservation exists, not that every node in vm_nodes has one. Adding a node after first deploy still needs --from vms or --force. Documented; pending live KVM validation on geekohive.

docs.title: 7. time.sleep() outside engine poll loops
docs.text:
File Usage start_cmd.py VIP wait loop (10s) stop_cmd.py, clean.py, restart.py shutdown polling start_if_needed_cmd.py VM start wait runner.py firewalld/service waits app.py TUI refresh (acceptable)

cluster.py and most of rancher.py correctly use self._sleep().

docs.title: 8. Glob-based resource discovery instead of ownership metadata
docs.text: clean, stop, start discover VMs via substring hints (harvester, rancher, edge, eib, rodeo) and glob patterns for disks. Fragile; can miss or over-match. ROADMAP Phase B1 (write rodeo:plan=<name> into domain XML) is the proper fix.

docs.title: 9. ansible-galaxy collection install on every deploy
docs.text: runner.py runs ansible-galaxy collection install on every deploy when install_collections=True. No marker/cache keyed on requirements.yml hash. Adds 10–30s per re-run. Listed in ROADMAP Phase D.

docs.title: 10. Silent inventory fallback masks definition errors
docs.text:
profiles/base.py:_load_inventory() catches all exceptions and returns None, falling back to static_vms. A broken definition.yaml can deploy the wrong topology with no clear error.

Remediation: Fail on ConfigError / FileNotFoundError; log warning on unexpected errors; only fall back for missing optional definition in dev.

docs.title: 11. ??cmd: resolver uses shell=True
docs.text: config.py:_resolve_secret_value() runs ??cmd: via subprocess.run(..., shell=True). Fine for advanced/CI; document as advanced-only. Low risk (local plans).

docs.title: 12. Documentation drift
docs.text: Doc Says Reality on main CLAUDE.md v0.10.3, 145 tests v0.12.0, ~190 tests CLAUDE.md profiles Missing harvester-2n 6 bundled profiles CONTEXT.md suse-edge on feature/suse-edge Merged to main CONTEXT.md "v0.10.x current" v0.12.0 CONTRIBUTING.md .github/workflows/integration.yml File does not exist

docs.title: 13. Two failing tests (brittle assertions, not logic bugs)
docs.text:
On Python 3.14 locally:

  • tests/test_self_update.py::test_successful_update_reports_fresh_version — Rich ANSI markup splits "0.11.2" across escape sequences
  • tests/test_up_cmd.py::test_up_with_custom_profile_deploys_in_place — same for "custom profile 'mycustom'"

Remediation: Strip ANSI in assertions or check independent substrings.

docs.title: 14. Instruqt validation queue entirely pending
docs.text: Per ROADMAP.md, no bundled profile has been end-to-end validated on an Instruqt builder since recent fixes (DNAT hook, network idempotency guard, harvester_auto_import default). Gate before any workshop track ships.

docs.title: Easy wins (low effort, high value)
docs.text: # Fix Effort Impact Status 1 Centralize rodeo_home() for all ~/.rodeo paths ~2h Fixes sudo/state/secrets split Done 2 Fix 2 brittle tests (strip ANSI from output) ~30min CI/local parity Done 3 Replace 2 time.sleep() in rancher.py with self._sleep() ~15min Cancellation correctness Done 4 Fix plan_cmd._flavor_of to use node flavor from inventory ~1h Correct edge-lab diffs Done 5 Port curl -4 download pattern to PXE + Harvester ISO tasks ~2h Instruqt reliability Done 6 Cache ansible-galaxy install with requirements hash marker ~2h Faster re-deploys Done 7 Sync CLAUDE.md version, test count, profile list ~30min Contributor accuracy Done 8 Fail loudly in _load_inventory on definition errors ~1h Better custom-profile DX Done 9 Log warning when _load_inventory falls back to static VMs ~30min Safer debugging Done 10 Structural test: no raw time.sleep in engine/ poll loops ~1h Enforce CLAUDE.md rule Done

docs.text:
• Event-driven DeployRunner with typed events — clean TUI/plain separation
  • Profile standardization in profiles/base.py — thin data classes, shared phase dispatch
  • Ansible idempotency in PXE network.yml (template for other roles)
  • Secret resolution fail-closed via validate_config()
  • Drift guards in tests/test_ansible_consistency.py
  • clean --refresh opt-in (no version strand on pinned hosts)
  • Live bare-metal validation for rancher, test, harvester-ha, harvester-2n

docs.text: File Why roles/kvm_host/tasks/libvirt.yml Modular daemon + NM guard — breaks Instruqt boot roles/vms/tasks/network_setup.yml virbr0 autostart:false intentional; recent idempotency guard roles/vms/defaults/main.yml OVMF paths, MACs, static IPs roles/pxe_server/ iPXE chain, config YAML perms, installer cmdline engine/cluster.py Bootstrap → VIP → etcd-gap join sequence engine/rancher.py Order-dependent API call sequence

  2. Fix failing tests + doc sync — quick hygiene

  4. plan_cmd flavor fix — correct diff for suse-edge

docs.title: Claude Code test plan: AWS single-host + Fleet multi-host
docs.text:
Executable checklist for Claude Code (or a human) against a laptop with AWS API access. Run steps in order. Stop on the first failed check. Do not invent CLI flags. Do not skip teardown unless the operator says so.

Related docs: testing, fleet, get-started.

docs.title: Agent rules
docs.text:
1. Work from a dedicated work dir on the laptop (not the rodeo-cli source tree for live deploys). Example: ~/rodeo-aws-tests.
  2. Prefer --yes / non-interactive flags. Never prompt the operator for secrets that should already exist in the environment.
  3. After each numbered step, record: PASS / FAIL + one line of evidence (command exit code, key stdout snippet, or path written).
  4. On FAIL: capture the failing command, stderr, and (for fleet) run rodeo fleet diagnose before asking the operator what to do.
  5. Never put AWS keys in YAML. Never print passwords from secrets.yaml or access sheets.
  6. Cost warning: each host is roughly i7i.8xlarge-class. Tear down when done.

docs.title: Operator fill-in (required before Part A / B)
docs.text:
Copy and set these once. Claude Code must refuse to start provision if any are empty.

Variable Example Your value AWS_REGION eu-central-1 SUBNET_ID subnet-… SG_IDS sg-… (allow 22, 8443, 30002) WORK_DIR ~/rodeo-aws-tests Fleet count 2 (min for multi-host)

Optional:

Variable Default Profile harvester Instance tier (single-host) recommended → i7i.8xlarge Marketplace Not needed: the default SLES 16 PAYG AMI requires no subscription

docs.title: Prerequisites (laptop)
docs.text:
mkdir -p "$WORK_DIR" && cd "$WORK_DIR"

# Creds: ~/.aws/credentials  OR  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
# Confirm identity (do not print secret keys):
aws sts get-caller-identity

python3 -m pip install -e '.[aws]'   # in your rodeo-cli checkout
# Or from a checkout: pip install -e '.[aws,dev]'
rodeo --version

Pass when: sts succeeds and rodeo --version prints a version.

docs.title: Part A: AWS single-host (rodeo up --target aws)
docs.text: Goal: one EC2 KVM host, remote lab deploy, NVMe host context, SSH helpers, cloud destroy.

docs.title: A1: Full single-host up
docs.text:
--no-deploy only seeds the lab on the laptop; it does not call EC2. Capacity (offerings + RunInstances DryRun) runs at provision time inside this command. If the region has no capacity, expect a clear error, no silent downsize.

You need provider.region, subnet_id, and security_group_ids in the seeded plan. Easiest path: seed once, edit the plan, then up.

cd "$WORK_DIR"
rodeo up --yes --profile harvester --no-deploy --dir ./single-host
# Edit ./single-host/rodeo-plan.yaml:
#   deployment_target: aws
#   provider:
#     type: aws
#     region: <AWS_REGION>
#     instance_tier: recommended
#     subnet_id: <SUBNET_ID>
#     security_group_ids: [<SG_IDS>]
#     ssh_user: ec2-user
#     volume_size_gib: 100

cd "$WORK_DIR/single-host"
rodeo up --yes --target aws --instance-tier recommended

Long-running (often 90–150+ min for harvester). Stay attached or poll logs (~/.rodeo/logs/… on the remote host via rodeo ssh).

Pass when: command exits 0 and success output shows Harvester / Rancher URLs. Fail-closed capacity errors at provision count as a valid gate (fix the region/type, re-run): not a product PASS until a successful deploy completes.

docs.title: A2: Verify host context + lab health
docs.text:
rodeo ssh primary -- 'findmnt -n -o TARGET,SOURCE | head -50'
rodeo ssh primary -- 'lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT'
# From the remote lab dir (path from success output / seeded lab):
rodeo ssh primary -- 'cd /root/lab 2>/dev/null || cd ~/lab; rodeo status --output json'

Adjust remote lab path if the seed used a different dir. Inspect plan/vars for Harvester disk sizing when NVMe is present (disk_gb 500 per Harvester node, 60 per Rancher node, flat, not scaled by node count, and storage.backend: nvme).

Pass when:

  1. Instance-store NVMe is mounted (or documented skip if type has no NVMe).
  2. rodeo status --output json shows healthy / expected phase completion.
  3. Nested guest disks live under the NVMe image_dir when backend is nvme.

docs.title: A3: Nested SSH targets
docs.text:
rodeo ssh primary/rancher -- 'hostname'
# Optional: Harvester node if present in ssh targets
# rodeo ssh primary/<node> -- 'hostname'

Pass when: SSH returns 0 without password prompts.

docs.title: A4: Tear down single-host cloud
docs.text:
# From the lab dir that holds the AWS plan / state on the laptop side:
rodeo destroy --cloud --yes

Pass when: EC2 instance tagged for this lab is terminated (confirm in AWS console or aws ec2 describe-instances).

docs.title: Part B: Fleet multi-host (AWS provision + fan-out)
docs.text:
Goal: count >= 2 EC2 hosts, fleet deploy → doctor → poll status → access → deprovision.

Use a new subdirectory so Part A state does not collide.

docs.title: B0: Write inventory
docs.text:
mkdir -p "$WORK_DIR/fleet-multi" && cd "$WORK_DIR/fleet-multi"

cat > workshop.yaml <<EOF
name: aws-fleet-smoke
lab:
  dir: /root/lab
  profile: harvester
  target: baremetal
  concurrency: 2
  ports:
    harvester: 8443
    rancher: 30002
defaults:
  ssh_user: ec2-user
provider:
  type: aws
  count: 2
  region: ${AWS_REGION}
  instance_tier: recommended
  # Or pin: instance_type: i7i.8xlarge
  subnet_id: ${SUBNET_ID}
  security_group_ids:
    - ${SG_IDS}
hosts: []
EOF

If instance_tier is rejected by fleet provision in your build, replace with instance_type: i7i.8xlarge.

Pass when: file exists; count: 2; hosts: []; no credentials in the file.

docs.title: B1: Provision hosts
docs.text:
cd "$WORK_DIR/fleet-multi"
rodeo fleet provision -f workshop.yaml

Pass when: exit 0; workshop.yaml hosts: has two entries with ssh / public_ip; SSH to both works:

rodeo ssh student-01 -- 'uname -a'
rodeo ssh student-02 -- 'uname -a'

docs.title: B2: Deploy (async fan-out)
docs.text:
rodeo fleet deploy -f workshop.yaml -j 2

Pass when: exit 0 quickly; workshop.job.yaml exists (chmod 600); host states are running or already ok.

docs.title: B3: Doctor (readiness)
docs.text:
Doctor runs rodeo on each host, and freshly provisioned hosts only get it from fleet deploy. Run it before deploy and it fails with rodeo: command not found.

rodeo fleet doctor -f workshop.yaml -j 2

Pass when: exit 0 (KVM / nested virt / tools / profile fit OK on every host).

docs.title: B4: Poll status until done
docs.text:
Repeat until every host is ok or failed (expect 90–150+ min):

rodeo fleet status -f workshop.yaml --output json
sleep 120

On any failed:

rodeo fleet diagnose -f workshop.yaml -o "$WORK_DIR/fleet-multi/diag" --output json
rodeo fleet retry -f workshop.yaml --failed-only

Pass when: all selected hosts reach lab-complete / job ok, or operator accepts documented failure after diagnose.

docs.title: B5: Access sheet
docs.text:
rodeo fleet access -f workshop.yaml --output json

Pass when: JSON lists per-host URLs (Harvester / Rancher ports) using public_ip; no passwords in the output.

Spot-check nested SSH:

rodeo ssh student-01/rancher -- 'hostname'

docs.title: B6: Deprovision
docs.text:
rodeo fleet deprovision -f workshop.yaml --yes

Pass when: tagged instances terminated. Note MVP gap: hosts[] may still list old IPs: edit or re-provision to refresh YAML (fleet.md).

docs.title: Results log (fill as you go)
docs.text:
Step Result Evidence Prereqs A1 A2 A3 A4 B0 B1 B2 B3 B4 B5 B6

Overall: PASS only if A1–A4 and B1–B6 pass.

docs.title: Claude Code one-shot prompt
docs.text:
Paste after filling the operator table:

Execute docs/examples/aws-fleet-claude-test-plan.md end-to-end.
Use WORK_DIR, AWS_REGION, SUBNET_ID, SG_IDS from my message.
Follow Agent rules: stop on first FAIL, no invented flags, no printing secrets.
Record the Results log table when finished. Tear down with A4 and B6.

docs.title: Example: AWS from a Mac, step by step
docs.text: This example starts from a Mac with nothing installed and ends with the rancher profile running on AWS: Rancher Prime on K3s plus three downstream clusters it manages (single-node K3s, single-node RKE2, 3-node RKE2). The Mac is only the control machine. The lab runs as nested VMs on one EC2 host. Any other profile works the same way: change --profile.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Requirement Why Check macOS with git and curl The installer clones the repo and fetches its own Python if needed git --version Homebrew Installs the AWS CLI and tmux brew --version AWS CLI 2.32.0 or later Older versions have no aws login aws --version tmux (recommended) Keeps the local rodeo up session alive if the terminal closes tmux -V AWS console access aws login reuses your console session (SUSE accounts: sign in with SUSE ID) You can open the AWS console

No Python install and no AWS access keys are needed.

Paste the command blocks below as they are. zsh does not treat # lines as comments when pasted interactively, so keep comments out of what you paste.

docs.title: Step 1: command line tools
docs.text:
xcode-select --install

If they are already installed, move on.

docs.title: Step 2: Homebrew
docs.text:
Skip if brew --version works.

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

docs.title: Step 3: AWS CLI and tmux
docs.text:
brew install awscli tmux
brew upgrade awscli
aws --version

brew upgrade only matters if the CLI was already installed. The version must be 2.32.0 or later.

docs.title: Step 4: install rodeo-cli
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avaleror/rodeo-cli/main/install.sh | bash

On a Mac the installer sets rodeo up as a control machine: no root, installed in ~/.local/share/rodeo-cli, command in ~/.local/bin/rodeo, with the [aws] extra. If the shell does not find rodeo:

echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
rodeo --help

To update later: rodeo self-update.

docs.title: Step 5: log in to AWS
docs.text:
Sign in to the AWS console in the browser first, then:

aws login
aws sts get-caller-identity

The first time, aws login asks for a default region if none is configured: enter eu-north-1, the region rodeo uses. Then it opens a browser page to confirm. get-caller-identity shows the account and role: check it before you create anything. The session lasts up to 12 hours, depending on the role. When it expires, run aws login again. The IAM principal needs the SignInLocalDevelopmentAccess managed policy (root users do not).

After the first login, recent AWS CLI versions offer to configure AWS skills and the AWS MCP server for AI coding agents. The lab does not need them: answer n to each prompt.

docs.title: Step 6: deploy
docs.text:
rodeo up --profile rancher --target aws --yes

rodeo picks the region (eu-north-1, or $RODEO_AWS_REGION), the default VPC public subnet and the profile's recommended instance, and writes them to the lab plan. It creates an SSH key and a security group that admits only your current public IP, launches the host, and builds the lab there in tmux. It ends by printing the Rancher URL and credentials. Expect 20 to 40 minutes for rancher.

Local files it creates:

Path Content ~/rodeo-labs/rancher/ Lab plan with region, subnet and instance. rodeo destroy needs it ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml Generated passwords (chmod 600) ~/.rodeo/ssh/labs/rancher/ This lab's own SSH key for the host and the lab VMs. Generated for this deployment and deleted by rodeo destroy --cloud

If the terminal closes during the deploy: tmux attach -t rodeo-rancher.

docs.title: Step 7: log in to Rancher
docs.text:
• URL: https://<host-public-ip>:30002
  • User: admin
  • Password: rancher_admin_password in ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml

rodeo status prints them again. On first login, confirm the server URL with the host IP. For SSH and day-2 commands, see the Rancher profile guide. Run them from ~/rodeo-labs/rancher or pass --config-dir ~/rodeo-labs/rancher.

docs.title: Step 8: tear down
docs.text:
The host terminates itself after provider.ttl_hours (default 6, see the dead-man switch). To delete it sooner:

rodeo destroy --cloud --yes --config-dir ~/rodeo-labs/rancher

docs.title: SSH key and shared accounts
docs.text:
Each deployment generates its own SSH key in ~/.rodeo/ssh/labs/<lab>/ and imports it as an EC2 key pair named rodeo-<lab>-<random>. Two users in the same AWS account never share or overwrite a key pair. rodeo destroy --cloud deletes the key pair and the local key. If the dead-man switch ends the lab first, the next rodeo up cleans them up.

The lab name still has to be yours. If someone else in the account has a live lab with the same plan name, rodeo up stops with:

lab 'rancher' already has instances in AWS (...) launched with key pair ..., whose private key is not on this machine

Do not destroy that lab: it is another user's. Change name: in ~/rodeo-labs/rancher/rodeo-plan.yaml (for example rancher-yourname) and run rodeo up again.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
Symptom Fix aws: unknown command 'login' AWS CLI older than 2.32.0: brew upgrade awscli session has expired or CreateOAuth2Token Run aws login again. A one-off CreateOAuth2Token error can just need a re-run MissingDependencyException The [aws] extra is missing: run the installer again no default VPC in <region> export RODEO_AWS_REGION=<region with a default VPC> and run rodeo up again Rancher UI or SSH times out Your public IP changed (new Wi-Fi, VPN). Re-run the rodeo up command: it moves the rule to your new IP and skips finished phases already has instances in AWS ... not on this machine Another user has a live lab with your plan name. See the SSH key section above rodeo: command not found Add ~/.local/bin to the PATH (step 4)

More in the runbook.

docs.title: Example: bare metal deployment
docs.text: This example walks through deploying the full harvester profile (3-node Harvester HCI + Rancher Prime) on a bare metal Linux host. The same steps apply to large cloud VMs with nested virtualization enabled.

docs.title: Host requirements
docs.text: Resource Minimum OS SLES 16 or Leap 16 (other Linux only with RODEO_ALLOW_ANY_KVM_HOST=1, unsupported) RAM 64 GiB (3 × 16 GiB Harvester + 8 GiB Rancher + host overhead) CPU 28 vCPU to spare Disk 900 GiB free in /var/lib/libvirt/images (or a dedicated second disk) KVM /dev/kvm present; no nested virt needed on bare metal

docs.title: Step 1: install rodeo-cli
docs.text:
On a clean SLES 16 / Leap 16 host:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avaleror/rodeo-cli/main/install.sh | bash

This clones the repo, sets up a Python environment internally, and links rodeo as a system command. No venv to activate, no PATH to set.

To install KVM packages, libvirt, ansible-core, and kubectl separately:

rodeo install-deps

rodeo up (Step 3) runs this automatically if deps are missing.

docs.title: Step 2: check the host
docs.text:
rodeo doctor

Expected output for a ready host:

Host facts
  ✓  root
  ✓  /dev/kvm
  ✓  nested virt        (not required on bare metal, shown as warning if absent)
  ✓  RAM     120 GiB total, 100 GiB available
  ✓  disk    900 GiB free in /var/lib/libvirt/images
  ✓  ansible-playbook
  ✓  ansible-galaxy
  ✓  kubectl
  ✓  python: libvirt
  ✓  python: lxml

Recommended profile: harvester (60 GiB needed, 100 GiB available)

docs.title: Step 3: deploy
docs.text:
rodeo up --profile harvester

rodeo up will: 1. Start a tmux session named rodeo-harvester so the deploy survives disconnects 2. Confirm the host checks pass 3. Generate ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml with random credentials 4. Seed the lab directory into ~/rodeo-labs/harvester/ 5. Self-escalate with sudo and start the deploy pipeline 6. Print login info when done

If your SSH session drops, re-attach to the running deploy:

tmux attach -t rodeo-harvester

Detach without stopping the deploy: Ctrl+b d.

Open a second tmux window (Ctrl+b c) to watch progress while the deploy runs:

rodeo watch         # split-panel TUI: phases + serial logs
rodeo logs harvester1   # or tail a single node

Total time: 90–150 minutes (most of it is Harvester iPXE install on nested KVM; bare metal is significantly faster).

docs.title: Step 4: log in
docs.text:
After rodeo up finishes:

  • Harvester UI: https://<host-ip>:8443
  • Rancher UI: https://<host-ip>:30002
  • Username: admin
  • Password: shown in the success output, or check ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml

docs.title: Using a dedicated second disk
docs.text:
If your host has a separate data disk (check with lsblk), configure it in rodeo-plan.yaml:

storage:
  device: /dev/nvme1n1    # your data disk: verify with lsblk first
  image_dir: /var/lib/libvirt/images

The kvm_host Ansible role will prepare and mount it before provisioning VMs.

docs.title: Redeploying after a clean
docs.text:
rodeo clean --all --yes --secrets   # destroy everything, wipe credentials
rodeo up --profile harvester        # fresh deploy with new credentials

docs.title: Multi-disk host with separate OS and data disks
docs.text:
Typical bare metal server: OS on /dev/nvme0n1, data on /dev/nvme1n1.

# rodeo-plan.yaml
storage:
  device: /dev/nvme1n1
  mount_point: /var/lib/libvirt/images
  image_dir: /var/lib/libvirt/images
  fs_type: xfs

The kvm_host role partitions the device, creates an XFS filesystem, and mounts it at image_dir if it is not already mounted.

docs.title: Day-2 operations
docs.text: Task Command Health check rodeo status SSH into a node rodeo ssh harvester1 Tail serial log rodeo logs harvester2 Graceful stop rodeo stop --all --yes Start after stop rodeo start --all --yes Destroy the lab rodeo clean --yes Full host reset rodeo clean --all --yes --secrets

docs.title: Example: Instruqt track image build
docs.text: This example shows how to build an Instruqt track with a pre-deployed Harvester lab. Attendees start with a running cluster: no waiting for iPXE install during the workshop.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Instruqt gives you a builder instance where you deploy the lab. You then Save a hostimage (snapshot). When an attendee starts a challenge, they get a copy of that image.

The key difference from bare metal: do not bake finalise into the hostimage. That phase enables VM autostart + libvirt-guests. If those are on when the image boots, nested KVM / virbr0 can race cloud-init and leave the Instruqt console on Please Wait. With deployment_target: instruqt, rodeo skips finalise automatically. Bring the lab up on every instance with rodeo start-if-needed in the track setup script instead.

docs.title: Host sizing on Instruqt
docs.text:
Use a generous builder (n2-standard-32 or ~40 vCPU) with nested virtualization enabled:

Resource Value RAM 128 GiB CPU 32–40 vCPU Disk 1–2 TB Nested virt Required

Request the geekohive machine type in the Instruqt sandbox config if you are using SUSE's Instruqt organization.

Guest vCPU budget: keep Σ guest vCPU ≤ ~70% of host logical CPUs. When you seed with deployment_target: instruqt (rodeo up on an Instruqt host, or rodeo up --deployment-target instruqt), rodeo applies host-aware presets, typically 6–8 vCPU / 20 GiB per Harvester node and 4 vCPU / 8 GiB for Rancher on a 32–40 vCPU builder. Override anytime with -P resources.harvester.vcpu=….

Guest disk cache defaults to writeback/threads on Instruqt (see libvirt.disk_cache in the plan reference): better nested cloud I/O than bare-metal none/native.

docs.title: Step 1: install rodeo-cli on the builder
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avaleror/rodeo-cli/main/install.sh | bash

This clones the repo, sets up a Python environment internally, links rodeo as a system command, and installs host dependencies (KVM, libvirt, ansible, kubectl).

docs.title: Step 2: set deployment target
docs.text:
Create your lab directory and set the target to instruqt:

rodeo new mylab --from harvester

Edit ~/.rodeo/profiles/mylab/rodeo-plan.yaml:

deployment_target: instruqt   # critical: skip finalise (never bake it into the hostimage)

Or use the bundled harvester profile directly and override at deploy time:

rodeo deploy -P deployment_target=instruqt

docs.title: Step 3: deploy the lab
docs.text:
rodeo up --profile harvester --yes

rodeo up immediately wraps itself in a tmux session named rodeo-harvester. This is critical on Instruqt: the browser tab can time out or close during a 90–150 minute deploy, and without tmux the process dies and leaves the host in a broken state.

If your Instruqt tab closes or times out, re-open the terminal tab and re-attach:

tmux attach -t rodeo-harvester

Detach without stopping the deploy: Ctrl+b d.

The finalise phase is skipped automatically when deployment_target: instruqt. That is what you want for a hostimage.

Verify the cluster is healthy before Save:

rodeo status

Expected: all 3 Harvester nodes Ready, VIP reachable, Rancher UI accessible.

docs.title: Step 4: hostimage checklist (before Save)
docs.text:
The success screen after deploy prints the same checklist. Confirm before you click Save:

Check Why Do not run rodeo deploy --finalise Bakes libvirt-guests + VM autostart → can hang boot / Please Wait firewall-cmd --list-ports includes 15778/tcp and 15779/tcp Instruqt terminal/editor agent ports systemctl is-enabled libvirt-guests is disabled Must stay off in the image Track setup will run rodeo start-if-needed Starts VMs + re-applies DNAT/nft on every boot

Optional: rodeo stop --all --yes before Save for cleaner nested guest disks (etcd/FS). Not required for agent connectivity.

Save captures disk state at click time. Running finalise after Save only changes the live builder; it does not update an already-saved hostimage. Re-Saving after finalise is how images get poisoned, don't do that for workshop hostimages.

docs.title: Step 5: take the Instruqt snapshot
docs.text: Use the Instruqt UI (Save hostimage) or API. At this point the cluster may still be running on the builder, but VMs must not be set to autostart in the image, which is correct.

docs.title: Step 6: track setup + verify on an attendee instance
docs.text:
Wire rodeo start-if-needed into the track's attendee boot/setup script (whatever runs when Instruqt starts a new instance from the hostimage). This is not optional for a healthy lab:

  • Nested VMs do not autostart (by design: no finalise in image).
  • The libvirt qemu hook that reapplies DNAT + guest_input accept only fires reliably on a genuine VM start, not on a cold hostimage boot with VMs left "as was."
  • start-if-needed is idempotent: starts host services + VMs if needed, then enforces nft rules.
rodeo start-if-needed

Check from inside the instance:

rodeo status

If VMs are shut off or UIs are unreachable after boot, the setup script likely omitted start-if-needed, add it and re-test; do not "fix" by baking finalise into a new Save.

docs.title: The firewalld timing constraint
docs.text:
The kvm_host Ansible role disables, stops, and masks firewalld during host prep (early in the build, before any VM exists). This is intentional: on SLES 16, firewalld integrates with NetworkManager via D-Bus, and cloud-init doesn't assign a zone to the external NIC, starting firewalld before that's sorted out can drop the Instruqt management connection.

firewalld itself is unmasked and started later, in the cluster phase, well before the snapshot, not by finalise. This is safe because that same step also runs, on Instruqt:

firewall-cmd --zone=public --change-interface=<ext-iface> --permanent

The --permanent flag writes the interface→zone mapping into firewalld's own persisted config. On a fresh attendee boot, firewalld reads that mapping directly instead of negotiating a live zone assignment with NetworkManager over D-Bus, which is what removes the race in the first place. So firewalld being enabled and running in the snapshot is expected and fine.

What actually matters before you snapshot: confirm this pinning step ran and picked the right interface. Check the deploy log for Instruqt: pinning <iface> to public zone..., and confirm with firewall-cmd --get-active-zones that your real management NIC shows under public. Re-check the same command on the first attendee boot from the snapshot, that's the actual test that the pinning held.

finalise must never be baked into the hostimage: it enables libvirt-guests + VM autostart, which races nested boot against the Instruqt agent and can leave the console on Please Wait.

docs.title: Credentials in the snapshot
docs.text:
Credentials are baked into the snapshot via ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml. All attendee instances share the same credentials. This is expected for workshop use: do not use production passwords.

Default credential location on the Instruqt instance:

cat ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml

docs.title: Console stuck on "Please Wait" after Save / start hostimage
docs.text:
The Instruqt terminal and editor tabs talk to the agent on the host (TCP 15778 and 15779), not to SSH alone. After cluster (or boot) unmasks and starts firewalld, those ports must be open on the public zone, otherwise a cold boot of the saved hostimage leaves the UI on Please Wait even when the OS is up.

rodeo opens them when deployment_target: instruqt (Ansible kvm_host firewall tasks + re-assert in _start_firewalld). On an older image that was built before that fix, recover once then re-Save:

sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-port=15778/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-port=15779/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
# or re-run: rodeo deploy --from cluster   # re-asserts ports for instruqt target

Also confirm you did not bake finalise into the image before Save (libvirt-guests enabled + VM autostart can stall network-online.target and block the agent). Prefer deployment_target: instruqt and rodeo start-if-needed on attendee boot instead of finalise-in-image.

docs.title: Cluster not reachable after attendee instance boots
docs.text:
1. Check if VMs started: virsh list --all
  2. If VMs are defined but not running, the track setup script probably did not run rodeo start-if-needed, run it now and add it to setup permanently. Do not bake finalise into a re-Save just to get autostart.
  3. If VMs are running but the Harvester/Rancher UI is still unreachable, this is almost always the nftables rules, not the VMs: the qemu hook that reapplies the DNAT + guest_input-accept rules does not reliably fire on hostimage boot. Run: 
    rodeo start-if-needed
    rodeo start --all --yes is not a substitute here, it starts VMs but does not touch nftables, so it won't fix this specific failure mode.
  4. Wire rodeo start-if-needed into the attendee boot/setup script so this self-heals on every instance start.

docs.title: iPXE install hangs during build
docs.text:
Instruqt nested KVM performance varies. If the iPXE install times out:

rodeo logs harvester1   # check where it is in the install
rodeo deploy --from cluster --force   # resume the cluster phase

docs.title: firewalld drops the Instruqt management connection
docs.text:
If you accidentally enabled firewalld before the snapshot and the builder instance loses connectivity:

  • Access the instance via the Instruqt emergency console
  • Run: systemctl stop firewalld
  • Restore connectivity, then re-snapshot with firewalld stopped

docs.title: Should I run rodeo deploy --finalise on Instruqt?
docs.text:
For hostimages: no. Keep finalise out of the image and use rodeo start-if-needed on boot.

finalise remains available for bare metal (and rare advanced cases with --finalise). If you enable it on a builder and then Save, you risk the next hostimage start sticking on Please Wait.

docs.title: Example: testing and CI
docs.text: This example covers running rodeo-cli in automated and testing contexts, from fast unit tests on any machine to full integration tests on a KVM host.

docs.title: Two tiers of testing
docs.text:
Tier What it covers Where it runs Time Unit / lint Config parsing, CLI surface, preflight logic, labseed, phase event model Any machine (no KVM) ~1 min Integration Full deploy pipeline: kvm_host → vms → pxe_server → cluster → rancher Self-hosted KVM host 1–3 h per profile

You need both. Unit tests catch regressions in Python code. Integration tests catch the real failures: disk sizing, network, iPXE chain, etcd bootstrap.

docs.title: Unit tests
docs.text:
Run on any OS: no KVM, no libvirt, no sudo needed:

pip install -e ".[dev]"
ruff check rodeo tests
pytest tests/ -v
# Ansible roles (optional locally; required in CI):
pip install "ansible-lint>=25" "ansible-core>=2.16,<2.19"
ansible-galaxy collection install -r rodeo/data/ansible/requirements.yml
ansible-lint rodeo/data/ansible

To keep your host clean (or when the host has a live libvirt that interferes with the stop/start tests), run the same checks in throwaway containers, as a non-root user: this mirrors the CI matrix exactly:

scripts/test-in-container.sh                 # Python 3.10 + 3.12, ruff + pytest
scripts/test-in-container.sh 3.12            # one version
scripts/test-in-container.sh 3.12 -- -k labinabox   # pass pytest args after --

What the unit tests cover:

Test file Area test_config.py Plan loading, Jinja2 rendering, -P overrides, ?? secret resolvers, validation test_runner.py Pipeline events, Instruqt guard, vars file generation test_ansible_consistency.py Profile ↔ Ansible defaults ↔ plan template alignment test_ansible_vars_contract.py Vars file keys match what Ansible roles consume test_pxe_integration.py Playbook order, pxe_server role, boot order, JOIN VIP guard test_cluster.py ClusterPhase poll loops, timeouts, node parsing test_rancher.py RancherPhase API call sequence, timeout handling test_plan_cmd.py rodeo plan diff output test_labseed.py Profile scaffolding, rodeo new, secrets generation test_preflight.py detect_host, recommend_profile, RAM/disk checks

docs.title: Test the CLI surface without KVM
docs.text:
rodeo up --no-deploy seeds a lab and runs preflight but stops before the deploy pipeline starts. Useful for validating the on-ramp flow in CI without a KVM host:

rodeo up --no-deploy --yes --profile test --dir /tmp/test-lab
ls /tmp/test-lab   # rodeo-plan.yaml + definition.yaml should be present
cat ~/.rodeo/secrets.yaml   # auto-generated if it did not exist

docs.title: Test config loading and overrides
docs.text:
# Dry-run: load and validate a plan, print what would deploy
cd /tmp/test-lab
rodeo plan

# Override a value and see it reflected
rodeo plan -P resources.harvester.memory_mib=20480

docs.title: Integration tests: manual
docs.text:
On a host that meets the bare metal requirements, run one profile at a time:

# Clean any previous state first
rodeo clean --all --yes --secrets --force-network

# Deploy and verify (--no-tmux skips the session wrap for scripted runs)
rodeo up --profile test --yes --no-tmux
rodeo status

# Clean up for the next run
rodeo clean --all --yes --secrets --force-network

docs.title: Profile test order (smallest to largest)
docs.text:
Run in this order to fail fast on smaller profiles before investing time in bigger ones:

  1. rancher (~10 min): fastest; validates the boot + Rancher path with no PXE
  2. test (~60 min): 2-node Harvester; validates the full iPXE chain
  3. harvester-ha (~90 min): 3-node Harvester; validates 3-member etcd HA
  4. harvester (~120 min): full lab; validates Rancher import on top of Harvester

docs.title: AWS live smoke
docs.text:
Manual checklist for infra-adaptive host context (provision or BYO). Needs AWS creds and nothing else: the default AMI (SLES 16 PAYG) needs no Marketplace subscription, and the recommended m8id.8xlarge supports nested virt.

# rodeo installed as a control machine (install.sh; see ../install.md)
# Provision path (recommended tier → m8id.8xlarge for harvester; region capacity checked first):
rodeo up --yes --profile harvester --target aws --instance-tier recommended
# Or BYO: SSH to an existing m8id.8xlarge (or similar), set deployment_target: aws, then:
#   rodeo up --yes --profile harvester

Testing your own changes: the instance installs rodeo-cli from GitHub, so a local working tree is invisible to it: and by default an already-bootstrapped host keeps the code it was first installed with. Push, then pass the ref:

rodeo up --yes --no-tmux --target aws --ref feat/my-fix

--no-tmux matters for scripted or agent-driven runs: without it up re-execs into tmux and the caller never sees the output. The remote log to read is /root/.rodeo/logs/aws-up.log on the host: far more informative than what surfaces locally.

Verify on the KVM host after kvm_host:

  1. resources.harvester.disk_gb is 500 and resources.rancher.disk_gb is 60, flat per-node floors, not scaled by node count (plan / vars)
  2. storage.backend: nvme and image_dir is mounted on instance-store NVMe (findmnt, lsblk)
  3. Guest disks live under that image_dir (not root EBS alone)
  4. Harvester VIP / rodeo status healthy; tear down with rodeo destroy --cloud --yes if provisioned

Unit coverage: tests/test_host_context.py, tests/test_kvm_host_nvme_storage.py.

Longer agent/ops checklist (single-host + fleet): aws-fleet-claude-test-plan.md.

docs.title: Integration tests: GitHub Actions (self-hosted runner)
docs.text: The integration workflow is at .github/workflows/integration.yml. It runs on a self-hosted runner with the labels self-hosted, kvm, sles16.

docs.title: Trigger manually
docs.text:
From the GitHub UI: Actions → Integration tests → Run workflow → select a profile or leave blank for all.

From the CLI:

# All profiles (nightly-style)
gh workflow run integration.yml

# One profile only
gh workflow run integration.yml -f profile=test

docs.title: What each job does
docs.text:
1. Pre-run cleanup: wipes whatever the previous run left (rodeo clean --all --yes --secrets --force-network), ignores failures so a broken previous run does not block the next one
  2. Deploy: rodeo up --profile <name> --yes
  3. Verify: rodeo status (asserts VMs are running and VIP is reachable)
  4. Post-run cleanup: always runs, even if deploy failed

max-parallel: 1 ensures only one profile runs at a time on the shared KVM host. fail-fast: false means all four profiles run even if one fails, giving you the full picture.

docs.title: Setting up a self-hosted runner
docs.text:
See CONTRIBUTING.md or the GitHub Actions runner docs for setup steps. The runner must have:

  • rodeo install-deps run once (KVM, libvirt, ansible, kubectl)
  • rodeo binary on PATH (via install-deps --link)
  • Passwordless sudo for the runner user

docs.title: Nightly schedule
docs.text: The workflow also runs nightly at 02:00 UTC via a cron trigger. Failed runs create a failed check on the main branch.

docs.title: Testing a specific Ansible role change
docs.text:
When you change an Ansible role (e.g. roles/kvm_host/tasks/firewall.yml), the unit tests do not catch regressions, they do not run Ansible. You must run a live integration test before merging.

Minimum regression for a role change:

rodeo deploy --from kvm_host --force   # re-run the changed role
rodeo status                           # verify the cluster still works

For the PXE chain (pxe_server role), the minimum is a full test profile deploy from scratch, the boot chain is only validated end-to-end when Harvester installs successfully.

docs.title: Testing definition.yaml changes
docs.text:
After editing a definition.yaml, validate it before deploying:

rodeo plan --profile mylab   # must succeed with no errors

Then test with the smallest matching profile:

rodeo clean --all --yes --secrets
rodeo up --profile mylab --yes
rodeo status

If the definition changes node count or IPs, the entire deploy must run from scratch, do not use --from cluster because the VM disk and DHCP lease changes come from the vms phase.

docs.title: Testing secret resolution
docs.text:
# Verify all ?? placeholders resolve
rodeo deploy --check

# Check placeholders without resolving anything (exit 2 if deploy would refuse)
rodeo plan

deploy --check runs the preflight suite (including secret validation) without starting any phase. It resolves ??key only and needs a trusted lab (rodeo trust). Placeholders must be written in rodeo-plan.yaml: -P and --paramfile values may not contain ??.

docs.title: Example workshop inventory
docs.text:
Copy to workshop.yaml and edit host SSH targets. Full reference: Fleet.

name: suse-virt-rodeo-emea
lab:
  dir: /root/suse-virt-workshop
  source: git:https://github.com/avaleror/suse-virt-workshop.git
  target: baremetal
  concurrency: 4
  ports:
    harvester: 8443
    rancher: 30002
defaults:
  ssh_user: root
hosts:
  - id: student-01
    ssh: 203.0.113.11
    public_ip: 203.0.113.11
    labels: { room: a }
  - id: student-02
    ssh: 203.0.113.12
    public_ip: 203.0.113.12
    labels: { room: a }

rodeo fleet doctor -f workshop.yaml
rodeo fleet deploy -f workshop.yaml -j 4
rodeo fleet status -f workshop.yaml
rodeo fleet diagnose -f workshop.yaml   # pull logs if a host fails
rodeo fleet retry -f workshop.yaml --failed-only
rodeo fleet access -f workshop.yaml

docs.title: AWS host-acquire (F4a MVP)
docs.text:
# workshop.yaml: hosts: [] until provision fills them
name: demo
lab:
  dir: /root/lab
  profile: harvester
defaults:
  ssh_user: ec2-user              # SLES 16 PAYG default AMI
provider:
  type: aws
  count: 2
  region: eu-central-1
  instance_type: m8id.8xlarge     # catalog 'recommended' for harvester
  # ttl_hours: 10                 # dead-man switch, default 6
  # ami omitted → newest SLES 16 PAYG
  subnet_id: subnet-…
  # security_group_ids: [sg-…]    # omit → rodeo manages one scoped to your IP
hosts: []

# rodeo installed on your laptop with install.sh (see ../install.md)
# Creds: aws login, ~/.aws/credentials, or AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
# SSH key: a new one per workshop in ~/.rodeo/ssh/labs/<workshop>/, deleted on deprovision
rodeo fleet provision -f workshop.yaml
rodeo fleet deploy -f workshop.yaml     # installs rodeo on each host, starts the lab
rodeo fleet doctor -f workshop.yaml     # needs rodeo on the host, so after deploy
rodeo ssh student-01
rodeo ssh student-01/rancher
rodeo fleet deprovision -f workshop.yaml --yes

See Fleet F4.

docs.title: Single-host AWS (rodeo up --target aws)
docs.text:
The provider: block is optional here: with none, rodeo picks eu-north-1 (or $RODEO_AWS_REGION), the default VPC subnet and the recommended instance. To set it yourself, it has the same shape:

deployment_target: aws
provider:
  type: aws
  region: eu-central-1
  instance_tier: recommended   # harvester → m8id.8xlarge (see instance_catalog)
  # instance_type: m8id.8xlarge  # or pin explicitly
  # SLES 16 PAYG by default; pin with ami: ami-… if needed
  # ttl_hours: 6                 # dead-man switch, default 6
  subnet_id: subnet-…
  # security_group_ids: [sg-…]   # omit → rodeo manages one scoped to your IP
  ssh_user: ec2-user
  volume_size_gib: 100            # root EBS; lab disks on NVMe via host_context

rodeo up --yes --profile harvester --target aws --instance-tier recommended
rodeo ssh primary
rodeo ssh primary/rancher
# tear down the EC2 host (not nested VMs alone):
rodeo destroy --cloud --yes

AWS is --target aws on the base topology (no separate *-aws profile). In Fleet workshop.yaml, never set lab.target: aws: use lab.target: baremetal on provisioned hosts.

docs.title: definition.yaml reference
docs.text:
definition.yaml is the topology declaration for a lab. It answers: which VMs exist, what are their names and IPs, in what order do they start, how are they networked, and which services are exposed on the host?

It does not contain resource sizing, credentials, or deployment target. Those live in rodeo-plan.yaml.

docs.title: Structure overview
docs.text:
definition:
  name:                    # lab name (usually matches plan name)
  description:             # human-readable label
  start_order:             # ordered list of VM names to start
  harvester_node_names:    # which of those are Harvester cluster members
  harvester_ready_count:   # how many must reach Ready before the cluster phase completes
  etcd_join_gap_seconds:   # pause before each non-first Harvester node starts

  network:                 # libvirt network config
  node_templates:          # NIC blueprints per VM flavor
  exposed_services:        # host port-forwards to guest services
  boot:                    # PXE/iPXE boot server config (Harvester only)
  storage:                 # lab storage layout
  components:              # high-level recipe description
  harvester:               # Harvester-specific cluster config
  rancher:                 # Rancher VM cloud-init + UI extensions to reconcile
  host_prep:               # host OS requirements (sysctls, SELinux, libvirt)
  nodes:                   # concrete VM declarations

docs.title: Full annotated example: 2-node Harvester (no Rancher)
docs.text:
apiVersion: 1.0   # increment for breaking schema changes

definition:
  name: suse-virt
  description: "2-node Harvester HCI cluster on nested KVM"

  # The ordered list of VMs to start during the cluster phase.
  # rodeo starts them in this order. Harvester1 always goes first (bootstrap node).
  start_order:
    - harvester1
    - harvester2

  # Which VMs in start_order are Harvester cluster members.
  # Drives: VIP wait, etcd gap application, node Ready count, ISO eject.
  harvester_node_names:
    - harvester1
    - harvester2

  # How many nodes must reach Ready before the cluster phase completes.
  # Must equal len(harvester_node_names) for a healthy cluster.
  harvester_ready_count: 2

  # Seconds to wait before starting each Harvester join node (not the first).
  # Prevents etcd join races when multiple nodes try to join simultaneously.
  # Do not reduce below 60s without live testing: 90s is proven safe.
  etcd_join_gap_seconds: 90

  network:
    name: default          # libvirt network name
    bridge: virbr0         # bridge interface on the host
    mode: nat              # nat | bridge (nat is standard for nested KVM)
    cidr: 192.168.122.0/24
    gateway: 192.168.122.1
    domain: rodeo.lab   # DNS domain for all lab VMs
    dhcp_range:
      start: 192.168.122.100
      end: 192.168.122.254  # static leases (.9–.13, .10 VIP) are outside this range

  # NIC blueprints. Each flavor defines the logical cables a VM of that type has.
  # The renderer (inventory.py) uses these to generate libvirt XML, DHCP leases,
  # iPXE scripts, and firewall rules.
  node_templates:
    harvester:
      flavor: harvester
      ssh_user: rancher
      infra_type: harvester    # tells stop/start this is a clustered Harvester node
      interfaces:
        - role: mgmt           # management NIC: PXE boot, VIP, Kubernetes API, etcd
          model: e1000
          pxe: true            # this NIC gets the iPXE boot entry
          ip_family: static    # DHCP static lease assigned from the node's ip field
        - role: storage        # Longhorn CSI traffic
          model: virtio
        - role: migration      # KubeVirt live migration
          model: virtio
        - role: service        # Kube-OVN primary uplink
          model: virtio
          count: 2             # generates service1 + service2 NICs

    rancher:
      flavor: rancher
      ssh_user: root
      infra_type: rancher      # tells stop/start this is a K3s/Rancher node
      interfaces:
        - role: mgmt
          model: virtio
          ip_family: static

  # Services reachable from outside the host. Each entry becomes a firewalld
  # port_forward (DNAT) rule on the public zone.
  exposed_services:
    - name: harvester-ui
      description: "Harvester dashboard and API"
      host_port: 8443
      guest_port: 443
      target: vip       # "vip" → the Harvester VIP; or a node name like "rancher"
      proto: tcp

    # Full lab (with Rancher) also adds:
    # - name: rancher-ui
    #   host_port: 30002
    #   guest_port: 30002
    #   target: rancher
    #   proto: tcp

  # iPXE boot server config (suse-virt profile only).
  # Drives the pxe_server Ansible role.
  boot:
    pxe:
      http_port: 8080
      http_bind: "{{ libvirt_network_gateway }}"   # binds on the virbr0 IP
      tftp_root: /var/lib/libvirt/dnsmasq
      http_root: /srv/harvester-pxe
      ipxe_efi_url: "https://boot.ipxe.org/x86_64-efi/ipxe.efi"

  storage:
    device: "/dev/nvme1n1"             # leave "" for single-disk hosts
    mount_point: /var/lib/libvirt/images
    fs_type: xfs
    libvirt_pool_name: default
    libvirt_pool_path: /var/lib/libvirt/images
    image_dir: /var/lib/libvirt/images

  # High-level recipe description. Used for introspection ("rodeo describe") and docs.
  components:
    - name: harvester-cluster
      description: "2-node Harvester HCI (RKE2 + Longhorn + KubeVirt + Kube-OVN)"
      nodes: harvester_node_names
      on_host: false
    - name: pxe-server
      description: "iPXE + HTTP server for diskless Harvester node boot"
      on_host: true
    - name: host-network-prep
      description: "libvirt network, firewalld DNAT, sysctls, SELinux for nested KVM"
      on_host: true

  # Harvester-specific cluster configuration embedded in per-node config ISOs.
  harvester:
    networks:
      mgmt:
        role: management
        description: "PXE boot, VIP, Kubernetes API, etcd, RKE2"
      storage:
        role: storage
        description: "Longhorn CSI traffic"
      migration:
        role: migration
        description: "KubeVirt live migration"
      service1:
        role: service
        description: "Kube-OVN primary uplink"
      service2:
        role: service
        description: "Kube-OVN secondary uplink"
    ntp_servers:
      - 0.pool.ntp.org
      - 1.pool.ntp.org

  # Host OS requirements. The kvm_host Ansible role applies these.
  # Change only if you know what you are doing: these values are tested on SLES 16.
  host_prep:
    sysctls:
      - net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=0
      - net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables=0
      - net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-arptables=0
      - net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=2
      - net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter=2
    selinux_mode: permissive
    libvirt:
      ovmf_code: /usr/share/qemu/ovmf-x86_64-4m-code.bin
      ovmf_vars_template: /usr/share/qemu/ovmf-x86_64-4m-vars.bin
      use_modular_daemons: true
    network:
      unmanaged_interfaces:
        - virbr0
      rp_filter_loose: true

  # Concrete VM declarations. Each node references a template and adds instance data.
  nodes:
    - name: harvester1
      template: harvester      # references node_templates.harvester above
      index: 1
      hostname: alpha           # alpha.rodeo.lab
      uuid: "1c5e1f38-1fb8-4f03-9eaa-12838f70faa1"
      ip: "192.168.122.11"
      config_iso_name: "harvester-config-node1"
      ssh_user: rancher
      interfaces:
        - role: mgmt
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:62:E1"
        - role: storage
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:63:E1"
        - role: migration
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:64:E1"
        - role: service
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:65:E1"
        - role: service
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:66:E1"
      # Legacy flat fields: kept for Ansible role compatibility during the Phase C transition
      mgmt_mac: "02:00:00:0D:62:E1"
      storage_mac: "02:00:00:0D:63:E1"
      migration_mac: "02:00:00:0D:64:E1"
      service1_mac: "02:00:00:0D:65:E1"
      service2_mac: "02:00:00:0D:66:E1"

    - name: harvester2
      template: harvester
      index: 2
      hostname: bravo
      uuid: "4e156918-3e00-44c2-bf47-0b532b3807c1"
      ip: "192.168.122.12"
      config_iso_name: "harvester-config-node2"
      ssh_user: rancher
      interfaces:
        - role: mgmt
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:62:E2"
        - role: storage
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:63:E2"
        - role: migration
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:64:E2"
        - role: service
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:65:E2"
        - role: service
          mac: "02:00:00:0D:66:E2"
      mgmt_mac: "02:00:00:0D:62:E2"
      storage_mac: "02:00:00:0D:63:E2"
      migration_mac: "02:00:00:0D:64:E2"
      service1_mac: "02:00:00:0D:65:E2"
      service2_mac: "02:00:00:0D:66:E2"

docs.title: apiVersion
docs.text: Schema version. Increment this when you make breaking changes to the definition format so consumers can detect incompatible files.

docs.title: Top-level cluster fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Notes name string yes Usually matches rodeo-plan.yaml name description string no Human-readable label start_order list yes VM names in the order they should start harvester_node_names list Harvester only Subset of start_order that are Harvester members harvester_ready_count int Harvester only Must equal len(harvester_node_names) etcd_join_gap_seconds int Harvester only Seconds before each join node starts (default 90)

docs.title: network
docs.text: Field Notes name libvirt network name: default for the standard NAT network bridge Host bridge interface: virbr0 for the default NAT network mode nat for nested KVM labs; bridge for direct host networking cidr The lab subnet. All VM IPs must be within this CIDR. gateway The host-side IP on virbr0. Usually .1 of the CIDR. domain DNS domain. libvirt's dnsmasq serves <hostname>.<domain> for all nodes. dhcp_range.start/end Dynamic DHCP pool. Static leases for lab VMs are assigned outside this range.

docs.title: node_templates
docs.text:
Templates define the NIC (interface) blueprint for a VM flavor. Individual nodes reference a template and list concrete MACs.

Interface roles:

Role Used for mgmt PXE boot, static DHCP lease, SSH, Kubernetes API, etcd storage Longhorn CSI traffic between nodes migration KubeVirt live migration traffic service Kube-OVN uplinks (primary and secondary)

Interface fields:

Field Notes model libvirt NIC model: e1000 (PXE-capable) or virtio (faster, no PXE) pxe true on the mgmt NIC tells the renderer to add iPXE boot entries ip_family static means a DHCP static lease is created for this NIC's MAC count Generates multiple NICs with the same role (e.g. service × 2)

infra_type on a template tells rodeo stop and rodeo start how to handle the VM:

Value Behaviour harvester Graceful ACPI shutdown in reverse start order; waits for RKE2 to drain rancher Graceful ACPI shutdown after Harvester nodes k3s, rke2 Downstream cluster nodes (rancher profiles), stopped like any other VM

Flavors (flavor on a template) pick the VM build: harvester (iPXE install), rancher and eib (cloud image + cloud-init), edge-node (SUSE Edge, booted from an Elemental image), and k3s-node / rke2-node (Leap 16 cloud image for the clusters Rancher provisions; sized by resources.k3s-node / resources.rke2-node in the plan).

docs.title: exposed_services
docs.text:
Each entry becomes a firewalld port_forward rule on the host's public zone.

Field Notes host_port Port on the host that external users connect to guest_port Port on the guest VM or VIP that the traffic is forwarded to target vip for the Harvester cluster VIP, or a node name from the nodes list proto tcp or udp

docs.title: nodes
docs.text:
Each node is a concrete VM. Fields:

Field Required Notes name yes Unique VM name. Must appear in start_order. template yes References a key in node_templates index yes Integer index used in naming (config ISO name, etc.) hostname no Short hostname (without domain). Generated from index if omitted. uuid no libvirt domain UUID. Generated deterministically if omitted. ip yes Static IP. Must be in network.cidr, outside dhcp_range. config_iso_name Harvester only Name of the Harvester config ISO file (without extension) ssh_user no OS user for rodeo ssh. Defaults to the template's ssh_user. interfaces yes List of NIC declarations with role and mac
